full_judgment:
2. The predecessor of respondents herein as pre-emptor filed miscellaneous Case No. 40 of 1994 under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act for pre-emption in the court of senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Keranigonj, Dhaka alleging, inter alia, that the case land comprising 11/4 decimals of land out of 8 decimals of land of C.S. Khatian Nos. 408 and 408/1, Hal khatian No. 267, c.s. and S.A Dag No. 292 originally belonged to Zinnat Ali, Zobar Ali and Sadar Ali and that Zobar Ali being the owner of 1/3 decimal of land out of 8 decimals of land died for leaving behind his wife, one daughter and 3 brother's sons, namely Abdul Kader, Abdul Hamid and Abdul Haque. Paribanu, the daughter of Sadar Ali sold 5 annas, 13 gondas, 1 kara and kranti land to the petitioner on 27.12.1978 and handed over possession, Zinnat Ali being owner of 1/3 decimal of land died leaving behind 3 (three) sons. Abdul Hamid sold his one 11 anna share to the petitioner on 2.12.1966 and handed over possession. Abdul Hoque died leaving behind his wife and 2(two) sons and they sold their one anna share to the petitioner on 28.6.1966 and handed over possession. Thereafter, Abdul Kader died leaving behind one son, i.e. opposite party No. 2, two daughters, i.e. opposite party Nos. 3-4 and wife opposite party No. 5. Opposite party No. 2 while possessing the case land sold the same to opposite party No. 1 showing the transfer to be an exchange. In fact, opposite party No. 2 sold the case land to opposite party No. 1 at a consideration of tk. 5,000/-(five thousand) only. Opposite party No. 1 is a stranger purchaser and the deed of exchange was created in order to defeat the right of pre-emption of the petitioner. The case land of schedule 'ka' and 'kha' are not equal in quantum, quality and price, and opposite part No. 1 did not serve any notice upon the petitioner as required by law. 

 3. Opposite party No. 1 contested the case by filing a written objection denying the material allegations made in the pre-emption application. The case of the opposite parties, in short, is that opposite party No. 1 got 'kha' schedule land comprising C.S dag No. 122 of khatian Nos. 1188, 507, 67 and Mution khatian No. 1/5 of Mouza Teghoria from the Government by way of permanent settlement and opposite party No. 1 was owning and possessing the 'kha' schedule land by mutating his name. Opposite party No. 2 requested the pre-emptor the purchase 'ka' schedule land, i.e. the case land or to exchange some other land with him, but the pre-emptor refused to accept the proposal of opposite party No. 2. Thereafter, opposite party No. 2 offered opposite party No. 1 to exchange decimals of land of Teghora Mouja, relating to mutation khatian no. 1/5 , c.s. Dag No. 122 with that of 11/4 decimals of land of Mouja Bayara, Khatian Nos. 408 and 408/1 (old), Hal Khatian No. 267 Dag No. 272.
